summary.title: CPU Device
summary.one_liner: The OpenVINO CPU plugin's supported precisions, half-precision and execution-mode hints, streams, caching, denormal and sparse-weight options for Intel x86-64 and Arm CPUs.
takeaways: Pass "CPU" as the device name to compile_model; multi-socket systems appear as a single CPU device.
Half-precision (bf16/f16) is used automatically in PERFORMANCE execution mode on supporting hardware; set inference_precision to f32 or use ACCURACY mode to avoid accuracy loss.
Multi-stream execution (num_streams > 1 or THROUGHPUT hint) gives each stream its own thread and group of NUMA-aligned physical cores.
Model caching via cache_dir reduces compile time and first-inference latency; sparse weights decompression needs int8 models, AMX, and channel counts that are multiples of 64.
summary.summary: This page is the reference for the OpenVINO CPU plugin, covering Intel x86-64 and Arm CPUs. It lists supported precisions (FP32, BF16, FP16, MXFP4, INT32, and quantized u8/i8/u1 on x86), explains how half-precision is chosen by default and how to override it with inference_precision or execution_mode hints. It also describes features such as automatic device selection, multi-stream execution, dynamic shapes, model caching, denormal handling, and sparse weights decompression, with code examples in Python and C++.
